subject: Agriculture
title: Household Food Waste
description: A short lesson to help you apply Household Food Waste.

hook.text: The average American household throws out $1,500 worth of food per year. Households are the biggest wasters.

buildup.text: We buy too much, cook too much, and forget leftovers. Poor meal planning drives most household waste.

discovery.text: Bread, fruit, and vegetables are the most wasted items in household bins globally.

twist.text: Smaller fridges correlate with less waste. Bigger storage encourages bigger buying—and bigger forgetting.

climax.text: Simple habits—shopping lists, using leftovers first, understanding dates—can cut household waste by half.

punchline.text: The biggest food waste problem isn't industry. It's your kitchen.

quiz.question: How much food does the average American household throw out annually?
